chunks: From him, from Humayd, from al-Hasan, from Ja'far ibn Sam'ah, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding the mukhtali'ah (woman who pays for divorce), he said: 'Her waiting period is the same as that of the divorced woman, and she observes her waiting period in her house, and the mukhtali'ah is in the position of the mubar'ah (woman who gives up her dowry for divorce).'
As for what was narrated - al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ibn Bukayr from Zurarah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he said: 'The waiting period of the mukhtali'ah is forty-five days.'

This report admits two interpretations: One is that if the mukhtali'ah is a slave woman who does not menstruate, and similar to her do menstruate, then her waiting period is forty-five days when her husband divorces her. The other interpretation is that the report is specific to a woman whose habit is to menstruate three times within this period, which is forty-five days. And there is no contradiction between the reports.

key_terms.المُخْتَلِعَة: Mukhtali'ah: A woman who initiates divorce by paying compensation to her husband
key_terms.الْحِيَض: Al-Hiyad: Plural of haidah, referring to menstrual periods
key_terms.الْعِدَّة: Al-'Iddah: The waiting period a woman must observe after divorce or death of husband before remarrying
key_terms.الْمُبَارِئَة: Mubar'ah: A woman who gives up her dowry for divorce, often used synonymously with mukhtali'ah
key_terms.الْمُطَلَّقَة: Al-Mutallaqah: A woman who has been divorced by her husband

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a woman who pays for her divorce (khula') in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi presents this narration from the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* to resolve the apparent discrepancy between the general rule that a *mukhtali'ah* (woman initiating divorce via *khula*) observes the same waiting period as a revocably divorced woman, and a specific report of forty-five days. He employs the principle of *takhsis* (specification) or contextual application, suggesting the forty-five days may apply to non-menstruating slaves or women whose three menstrual cycles naturally conclude within that timeframe, thereby harmonizing the texts without contradiction.
